meta.title: Political psychology knowledge network, c. 1950-2026
meta.description: Key works and debates in political psychology: belief systems and political knowledge, motivated reasoning, emotion and affective intelligence, personality and values, authoritarianism and threat, social and partisan identity, affective polarization, framing and persuasion, heuristics and elite cues, misinformation and conspiracy beliefs, moral foundations, the psychology of left and right, biology and genetics, trust and tolerance, socialization, leaders and perception in international politics, intergroup attitudes, and experimental methods. Works shared with the other maps are imported from them; others are top-cited 2006-2026 articles selected via Crossref (political psychology and political science journals) and anchoring books and classics. Direction: source (later or dependent work) -> target (earlier or anchoring work).

edge_types.builds_on: source extends or relies on target's argument or evidence
edge_types.challenges: source contests target's claim, mechanism or evidence
edge_types.qualifies: source adds a scope condition or moderating factor to target
edge_types.extends_to_new_case: source applies target's logic to a new population, period or domain
edge_types.synthesizes: source integrates target with other work
edge_types.mechanism_tested_by: source tests a mechanism implied by target

meta.verification: Repo works come from the user's Zotero library. Works imported from the other maps keep their verification. Crossref-selected works take title, authors, year, venue and DOI from Crossref records. Anchors are checked in Crossref separately; see each node's `verified` field. One-line claims for non-repo works are my summaries.
